questions.question_text: A 45 year old woman during the course of her therapy says that she is happy but the whole world is depressed. She is displaying the following defence mechanism

Selective abstraction is not a defense mechanism (instead, it is a CBT term). Externalisation and overgeneralisation are types of cognitive distortion listed in the context of CBT (they are not listed by Freud or neo-Freudians as 'defense mechanisms'). Johnstone, E. C., Cunningham Owens, D. G., Lawrie, S. M., Sharpe, M., & Freeman, C. P. L. (2004). Companion to psychiatric studies (7th ed., pp 311-314); Rycroft, C. (1995). questions.question_text: According to Kernberg, the psychodynamic understanding of borderline personality disorder did not include
questions.explanation:
As per Kernberg, Diagnoses of Borderline personality Organisation are based on three categories of criteria. The first, and most important, category, comprises two signs: the absence of psychosis (i.e., the ability to perceive reality accurately) and impaired ego integration - a diffuse and internally contradictory concept of self. The second category is termed "nonspecific signs" and includes such things as low anxiety tolerance, poor impulse control, and an undeveloped or poor ability to enjoy work or hobbies in a meaningful way. The third category is the presence of "primitive defenses." The main one is splitting, in which a person or thing is seen as all good or all bad. Other primitive defenses cited include magical thinking, omnipotence, projection of unpleasant characteristics in the self onto others and projective identification.
Oxford textbook of psychotherapy,2007,p-292

questions.explanation: The Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) is a 10‐item self‐report screening tool for postnatal depression.

questions.question_text: The last stage according to Prochaska and Diclemente model of change of behaviour is
questions.explanation:
Maintenance is the final stage where new behaviours are sustained.
Handbook of Alcoholism, Zernig et al., 2000.

questions.question_text: A 40 year old man who is a heavy drinker does not recognise that he requires to change, does not accept his problem drinking. Regarding his motivation to change he is in the stage of
questions.explanation: In the precontemplation stage, the individual is not yet acknowledging that there is a problem to change.

questions.question_text: According to current evidence base, the treatment of choice for pathological crying is:
questions.explanation:
SSRIs such as citalopram are first‐line for pathological laughing and crying.
Pretzel TA et al. CNS Drugs 2008.

questions.question_text: Neuroimaging studies in patients with OCD show

options.text: Hypermetabolism in left orbital gyrus and both caudate nuclei
Asymmetries in blood flow in limbic system
Reduced metabolism in left orbital gyrus

correct_answer.text: Hypermetabolism in left orbital gyrus and both caudate nuclei

correct_answers.text: Hypermetabolism in left orbital gyrus and both caudate nuclei

questions.explanation: PET studies show hypermetabolism in the orbitofrontal cortex and caudate nuclei in OCD.

questions.question_text: NINCDS-ADRDA criteria for diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease does not include

options.text: deficits in two or more areas of cognition
progressive worsening of memory and other cognitive functions

questions.explanation: Age at onset 40–90 is part of the criteria; the incorrect option is the only one not included in the standard criteria.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is most common in delirium?
questions.explanation: Disturbance of the sleep–wake cycle is one of the cardinal features of delirium.

questions.question_text: The mechanism of action of Rivastigmine is

options.text: irreversible inhibition of the enzyme acetylcholinesterase
reversible inhibition of the enzyme acetylcholinesterase
(IR)reversible inhibition of the enzyme acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase
reversible inhibition of the enzyme acetylcholinesterase and butrylcholinesterase

correct_answer.text: reversible inhibition of the enzyme acetylcholinesterase and butrylcholinesterase

correct_answers.text: reversible inhibition of the enzyme acetylcholinesterase and butrylcholinesterase

questions.explanation: Rivastigmine pseudo‐reversibly inhibits both acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase.

questions.question_text: You see a 12 year old boy with Tourette's syndrome, who also has hyperkinetic disorder. The most effective treatment for this boy would be
questions.explanation:
Atomoxetine (a noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor, NARI) is recommended for ADHD with comorbid tics.
NICE guidelines for ADHD, 2008

questions.question_text: According to ICD-10 the following is not a feature of Dissociative disorder

options.text: Convincing association between onset and need
Amnesia can be too extensive to be explained by intentional simulation
Can present as loss of awareness of immediate surroundings
No temporal relationship between the onset and stressful events
Physical disorder may be present giving rise to other symptoms

correct_answer.text: No temporal relationship between the onset and stressful events

correct_answers.text: No temporal relationship between the onset and stressful events

questions.explanation: ICD‐10 requires a clear temporal association between stressful events and onset of dissociative symptoms.

questions.question_text: A 36 year old lady has been frequently seeing her dentist with pain and tingling sensation around her jaw for the last two years. On each occasion, the examination did not reveal any abnormality. The most likely diagnosis in this lady is
questions.explanation: This presentation is most consistent with a somatoform pain disorder—chronic pain without physical pathology.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most common feature in delirium?
questions.explanation: Disturbed sleep–wake cycle is a hallmark of delirium.

questions.question_text: Which of the following psychotherapies utilises reciprocal role reversal
questions.explanation: Psychodrama, as developed by Moreno, uses reciprocal role reversal among other techniques.

questions.question_text: Asperger's syndrome differs from childhood autism in, Choose one answer.
questions.explanation: Unlike in autism, intellectual ability and syntactical speech are normal in Aspergers syndrome

questions.question_text: A 70 year old lady was admitted to general hospital being severely unwell. Two days later she began complaining to her relatives that staff are not treating her well and poisoning her food. She also reports seeing spiders crawling under the bed, most possibly placed there by the Nurses. the most likely diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Increasing old age, dementia, visual impairment and severe medical illness are important risk factors for delirium. An acute onset, elderly and concurrent severe medical illness suggests delirium in this case.

questions.question_text: The following psychotropic medication is excreted mostly through the kidneys and is considered as unsafe in a person with severe renal failure
questions.explanation: Amisulpiride is mainly excreted by the kidneys and has minor hepatic metabolism. The Maudsley guidelines have advocated against the use of Sulpiride and Amisulpiride in someone with renal impairment. They advise to use Haloperidol (if typical antipsychotics are to be used) and Olanzapine (Atypical Antipsychotics are to be used).

questions.question_text: The risk of alcoholism in children of Alcoholic parents compared to children of non-alcoholic parents is
questions.explanation: Though the most popularly reported risk of Alcoholism in children of alcoholic parents is 4 times the risk in children of non-alcoholic parents, a recent study which has adjusted for the risk of other illicit drug dependence has found the risk to be around 2–3 times higher in children of alcoholic parents compared to children of non-alcoholic parents.

questions.question_text: The ICD-10 diagnosis for conversion disorder includes the following

options.text: Severe pain is a predominant symptom
Some clue that the person is feigning their symptoms

questions.explanation: Dissociative (conversion) disorders tend to remit after a few weeks or months, and ICD-10 includes only disorders of voluntary motor or sensory function that are not better explained by another condition.

questions.question_text: The first line of treatment of an 8 year old child with hyperkinetic disorders without any co-morbidities but severe impairment is
questions.explanation: NICE guidelines recommend methylphenidate as the first-line pharmacological treatment for ADHD in children without significant comorbidities.

questions.question_text: The prevalence of psychotic disorders in prisons compared to the general population is
questions.explanation: The prevalence of psychotic disorders in prison is between 2–15% and approximately 20 times greater than that for adults in the general population.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is recognised to cause schizophrenia like psychosis
questions.explanation: Huntington's disease can present with florid schizophrenic symptoms even before the diagnosis is apparent.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cognitive function is less impaired in patients with schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: Language, motor and visuospatial functions are less consistently impaired in first-episode schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: The Scale that is used to measure the severity of EPSE is
questions.explanation: Simpson Angus Scale is specifically used to measure severity of extrapyramidal side effects.

questions.question_text: A 63 year old inpatient has developed deviation of mouth and is drooling saliva from the corner of his mouth. He is still able to frown his forehead. He has recently completed a course of antibiotics for a middle ear infection. What is the likely underlying pathology?

options.text: Facial nerve palsy (upper motor neuron lesion)

correct_answer.text: Facial nerve palsy (upper motor neuron lesion)

correct_answers.text: Facial nerve palsy (upper motor neuron lesion)

questions.explanation: In an upper motor neuron lesion the forehead is partially spared, allowing frowning while lower facial muscles are weak.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is now regarded as the standard screening test for alcohol use with a high sensitivity and specificity?
questions.explanation: The AUDIT (Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test) is the standard 10-item screening tool with sensitivity and specificity over 90%.

questions.question_text: A subcultural explanation rather than a biological one in learning disabilities is most accounted for by:

options.text: An even spread of LD across different socio-economic groups of the population
Parents with a child with LD have lower IQ

questions.explanation: ‘Sub-cultural’ learning disability refers to the normal lower end of the IQ distribution (mild LD, IQ 50–70) without organic causes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is less commonly seen in Pediatric Autoimmune Neuropsychiatric disorder associated with Streptococcal infection
questions.explanation: PANDAS presents with OCD and/or tics, ADHD, anxiety, but hallucinations are not characteristic.

questions.question_text: The following is true regarding Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors

options.text: Galantamine does not have action on the nicotinic receptors
Ginkgo biloba has the same efficacy as Donepezil in the treatment of Alzheimer's dementia
Memantine is an agonist at NMDA receptors
Rivastigmine is given as a once daily dose
Donepezil is metabolised by 2D6 and 3A4 enzymes of the cytochrome P450 system

correct_answer.text: Donepezil is metabolised by 2D6 and 3A4 enzymes of the cytochrome P450 system

correct_answers.text: Donepezil is metabolised by 2D6 and 3A4 enzymes of the cytochrome P450 system

questions.explanation: Donepezil and galantamine are metabolised by CYP2D6 and CYP3A4, leading to potential drug interactions; rivastigmine has minimal P450 metabolism.

questions.question_text: A 22 year old lady presents with severe OCD with obsessions of dirt and compulsion of washing. She is currently neglecting herself and though she is eating one meal a day, she has not been drinking for fears of contamination. The best treatment for her would be
questions.explanation: Severe self-neglect and risk due to OCD warrant inpatient admission for combined pharmacotherapy and CBT.

questions.question_text: The following disorder is found only in girls.
questions.explanation: Rett's syndrome occurs almost exclusively in females and involves regression of speech and hand skills.

questions.question_text: The following neonatal outcomes are seen in newborns born to anorexic mothers
questions.explanation: Infants of mothers with eating disorders have significantly lower birth weight and smaller head circumference.

questions.question_text: A 15 year old girl presents with Anorexia nervosa. The current best evidence for treatment is
questions.explanation: NICE recommends family interventions directly addressing the eating disorder for adolescents with anorexia nervosa.

questions.question_text: The percentage of exhibitionists without a previous conviction for sexual offences is
questions.explanation: About 26% had at least one conviction; hence approximately 74%–80% have no prior convictions.

questions.question_text: One of the most evidence based treatment for reducing Tics in Tourette Syndrome is
questions.explanation: Haloperidol has the strongest evidence among pharmacological treatments for tic reduction in Tourette’s syndrome.

questions.question_text: What treatment would you use for a patient with severe symptoms of pre-menstrual syndrome?
questions.explanation: SSRIs have the strongest evidence for effectiveness in treating severe PMS symptoms.

questions.question_text: When assessing a patient with the features of early dementia which of the following would suggest a sub-cortical rather than a cortical cause?
questions.explanation: Subcortical dementias typically preserve calculation ability until late in the illness.

questions.question_text: Poor prognostic factors for Anorexia nervosa include all the following except
questions.explanation: Younger age of onset is associated with better outcomes, so it is not a poor prognostic factor.

questions.question_text: The following route of cocaine use leads to a onset of action lasting for about 20-30 minutes
questions.explanation: Intranasal cocaine produces euphoria in 3–5 minutes with effects lasting 15–30 minutes.

questions.question_text: The current best evidence for the treatment of dementia associated with Parkinson's disease is
questions.explanation: Cochrane review shows rivastigmine has the most evidence for improving cognition and daily function in Parkinson’s dementia.

questions.question_text: A 39 year old female patient has had recurrent depressive episodes in the past and one episode of hypomania. The best medication to prevent relapse for her is:
questions.explanation: Lamotrigine has evidence for preventing depressive relapses and is preferred in Bipolar II disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following treatments for multiple sclerosis is most likely to lead to depression?
questions.explanation: Interferon-beta is associated with depression and suicidal thoughts in multiple sclerosis patients.

questions.question_text: The scale used to screen for cognitive impairment in people with Downs syndrome is
questions.explanation: The DMR (Dementia Questionnaire for Persons with Mental Retardation) is one of the validated scales for dementia screening in intellectual disability.

questions.question_text: You are seeing the parents of a 26 year old gentleman currently under your care. He has been diagnosed with Schizophrenia and his parents want to know his prognosis. What type of schizophrenia has the best prognosis out of the following
questions.explanation: Paranoid schizophrenia, especially with an acute onset and fewer negative symptoms, is associated with a better prognosis.

questions.question_text: The antidepressant of choice used in the treatment of moderate depression in a patient who has Myocardial infarction is
questions.explanation: Sertraline has the best safety and evidence profile for use after acute myocardial infarction.

questions.question_text: Massed negative practice is used in which of the following conditions
questions.explanation: Massed negative practice is a behavioural intervention in which tics are practiced until fatigue, used for Tourette's syndrome.

questions.question_text: A 20 year old man presents to the A&E with PCP intoxication. The signs / symptoms that he can present with include
questions.explanation: PCP intoxication includes paranoid ideas, nystagmus, ataxia, hypertension, and analgesia (decreased pain sensitivity), not increased sensitivity.

questions.question_text: The following statements are valid in the use of Automatism as a defense for murder

options.text: Murder should have ideally occurred within 2 hours of sleep
The person can partially recollect the act on the following morning
The person recollects the act as if it had occurred in his dream
The person can clearly recollect the act in the morning after the murder
The person wakes up in the middle of the night screaming and in a panic during the act

correct_answer.text: Murder should have ideally occurred within 2 hours of sleep

correct_answers.text: Murder should have ideally occurred within 2 hours of sleep

questions.explanation: In automatism there is complete or severe amnesia for the act, though sometimes partial and confused recall occurs.

questions.question_text: What is not true about Varenicline tartarate

options.text: Only contraindication is hypersensitivity to the drug
It is a nicotinic receptor antagonist

correct_answer.text: It is a nicotinic receptor antagonist

correct_answers.text: It is a nicotinic receptor antagonist

questions.explanation: Varenicline is a partial agonist at α4β2 nicotinic receptors, not an antagonist.

questions.question_text: A 41 years old pharmacist presents with a history of disabling anxiety symptoms. He has recently been made redundant from his job due to certain concerns from his employer. Which of the following symptom is likely to point towards a benzodiazepine withdrawal than a functional anxiety state?
questions.explanation: Perceptual disturbances such as sensory hypersensitivity are relatively specific to benzodiazepine withdrawal.

questions.question_text: The following disorder results due to deletion of the chromosome of maternal origin
questions.explanation: Angelman syndrome arises from microdeletion of the maternally inherited chromosome 15q11–13 region.

questions.question_text: The sign / symptom least likely to be experienced by a person taking MDMA is
questions.explanation: MDMA is not classically hallucinogenic; it produces increased energy, empathy, and can cause anxiety or paranoia.

questions.question_text: The most common symptom that appears on withdrawal from Benzodiazepines is
questions.explanation: The most common benzodiazepine withdrawal symptom is rebound insomnia, occurring within days of discontinuation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is less likely an outcome of childhood onset conduct disorder

options.text: Have less number of children themselves

correct_answer.text: Have less number of children themselves

correct_answers.text: Have less number of children themselves

questions.explanation: Childhood-onset conduct disorder is associated with increased numbers of children, not fewer.

questions.question_text: In the treatment of opiate withdrawal in a person having low BP the following is given
questions.explanation: Lofexidine causes less hypotension than clonidine and is recommended for opioid detoxification when hypotension is a concern.

questions.question_text: Which of the following anticonvulsant has the strongest evidence to suggest that it can be used to augment clozapine in treatment-resistant schizophrenia
questions.explanation: Lamotrigine has evidence as an augmenting agent in partial responders to clozapine.

questions.question_text: A 15 year old boy presents with a moderate depressive illness. He is otherwise fit and intelligent and does not have suicidal ideas or plans. The treatment of choice for this boy would be
questions.explanation: For moderate to severe depression in adolescents, NICE recommends concurrent psychological therapy (e.g., CBT) with an SSRI.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a false statement regarding functional enuresis in children

options.text: Cannot occur as a complication of a psychiatric illness
Maybe nocturnal or diurnal in nature
Parental attitude has no aetiological role
Part of Helman's triangle for predicting future violence

correct_answer.text: Parental attitude has no aetiological role

correct_answers.text: Parental attitude has no aetiological role

questions.explanation: Rigid toilet training and negative parental attitudes are known etiological factors in functional enuresis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following has the least potential to cause psychological and physical addiction?
questions.explanation: LSD has minimal potential for physiological or psychological dependence compared with other listed substances.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a test of heterogeneity in Meta-analysis
questions.explanation: Cochran’s Q test (a chi-square test) is used to detect heterogeneity among studies in a meta-analysis.

questions.question_text: An evaluation of a new screening questionnaire for depression in primary care is conducted. The most important single feature of this questionnaire that would encourage you to use it is:

options.text: It has Positive Predictive Value of 20%
It is validated in different languages

questions.explanation: High sensitivity is crucial for a screening instrument to correctly identify the majority of true cases.

questions.question_text: What is the range of values for a correlation coefficient
questions.explanation: The correlation coefficient varies from –1 (perfect negative) through 0 (no relationship) to +1 (perfect positive).

questions.question_text: Expert opinions form what grade of Evidence
questions.explanation: Expert committee reports/opinions and clinical experience (evidence level IV) are classified as Grade C evidence by NICE.

questions.question_text: Cronbach’s alpha measures which of the following
questions.explanation: Cronbach’s alpha assesses the internal consistency of items within a scale.

questions.question_text: The statement for reporting Meta analysis is provided by
questions.explanation: The QUOROM (Quality of Reporting of Meta-analyses) statement provides guidelines for reporting meta-analyses.

questions.question_text: The most appropriate measure to explain about treatment response of a medication to a patient would be
questions.explanation: Number needed to treat (NNT) is the number of patients who need to be treated for one to benefit compared with a control.

questions.question_text: The database that provides systematic coverage of the psychological literature from the 1800s to the present is
questions.explanation: PsycINFO covers psychological literature systematically from the 1800s to present.

questions.question_text: The cost of forgoing an established treatment whilst opting for a new treatment is termed as
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of benefits foregone by choosing one intervention over the next best alternative.

questions.question_text: A researcher wants to evaluate the use of Magnetic resonance imaging as a screening test to identify cases of Alzheimer's dementia. They would confirm the correct diagnosis of Alzheimer's dementia by post mortem examination of the brain. Which of the following study designs would be the most appropriate for such a study?
questions.explanation: Cross-sectional studies are most appropriate when evaluating a screening test against a gold standard at a single point in time.
